claims.text: Formation of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
Crystal-structure selection in these nanoparticles is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
Thermodynamic and kinetic factors determine the balance among phase separation, elemental segregation, and single-phase solid-solution stability.
The initial material is a single-phase solid solution.
Composition and processing conditions will be varied in a controlled manner.
Certain compositions and processing conditions will produce phase separation relative to the initial single-phase baseline.
Certain compositions and processing conditions will produce elemental segregation relative to the initial single-phase baseline.
Certain compositions and processing conditions will produce uncontrolled particle morphology relative to the initial single-phase baseline.
Compositional and processing boundaries exist beyond which phase separation, elemental segregation, or uncontrolled particle morphology occurs.
The specific thermodynamic and kinetic factors governing formation and crystal-structure selection are not understood.
Phase composition, elemental distribution, and particle morphology will be measured during systematic variation of composition and processing conditions.
Persistence of a single-phase solid solution under conditions predicted to cause separation, segregation, or uncontrolled morphology would falsify the hypothesis.
